sources.entry: Hyphanet - Anonymously share files, browse and publish _freesites_ (web sites accessible only through Hyphanet) and chat on forums. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 Java

summary.one_liner: Fred is the Java reference daemon for Freenet, a peer-to-peer, encrypted, decentralized datastore for censorship-resistant communication and publishing.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Freenet as peer-to-peer software that provides a distributed, encrypted, decentralized datastore on which websites and applications such as forums and chat are built. Fred ("Freenet REference Daemon") is the codebase that runs the node. The README covers building with the included Gradle wrapper (./gradlew jar) or with Ant, running unit tests with Gradle, and testing a custom build by replacing freenet.jar in an existing Freenet directory. It also explains how installers are produced in separate repositories (Linux/macOS/*nix and Windows) and how new dependencies must be published on Freenet itself and registered in dependencies.properties. Integration tests are marked as TODO in the README.
use_cases: hosting freesites on a decentralized network
how_to_run: mkdir -p lib; (cd lib && grep -o CHK.* ../dependencies.properties | xargs -P16 -I {} bash -c 'fcpget -v {} "$(echo {} | sed s,^.*/,,)"')
notable: Dependencies are distributed through Freenet itself (CHK keys in dependencies.properties) rather than a public package repository
Windows installer is code-signed free of charge via SignPath.io, per the README
Builds with a committed Gradle wrapper that verifies the checksum of the downloaded archive
Installers are built from separate hyphanet repositories
caveats: Integration tests are not documented (README says TODO)
Building the dependencies from source requires fetching them through Freenet with fcpget, which is an extra setup step
Licensing notes say some plugins are GPL3 and some bundled code is Apache 2.0 or BSD
